Treat as expected, not findings:

- Fictional data in tests and demo fixtures (e.g. "postgres://u:p@ep-demo.neon.example/db", "e2e-only-secret-not-used-anywhere-else"). These are not credentials.
- packages/parsers uses template.innerHTML on an inert <template> element to strip HTML from JSON-LD descriptions. Template content doesn't execute scripts or load resources.
- 'unsafe-inline' in the web app's script-src: Next.js App Router injects inline bootstrap scripts; there's no user-controlled HTML rendering (React escapes output).
- Requests without an Origin header are allowed by assertTrustedOrigin by design (they carry no ambient browser cookies).
- chrome-extension:// origins are allowed by assertTrustedOrigin by design (the extension calls the API with the user's session).
- Rate-limit and denial-of-service concerns (excluded by default).
- apps/web/src/app/layout.tsx uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML for THEME_SCRIPT (apps/web/src/components/nav.tsx): a fixed string constant that reads localStorage to set the theme before paint. No user, page or model data reaches it.
- Coach-share recipients reading another account's application in apps/web/src/server/coach.ts: this is the owner-approved, consented exception to owner-only reads (see SECURITY.md). Findings there should be about missing checks (revocation, acceptance, field exclusions), not the existence of the read.
